study_identification_part.si4_title: Individualized cerebellar damage predicts the presence of behavioral disorders in children with brainstem tumors

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Investigate cerebellar damage patterns resulting from pediatric brainstem tumors and their associations with behavioral disorders by building a normative model of cerebellar lobular volumes and evaluating prediction of behavior using total outlier count (tOC) and lobular volumes.

caa6_deviation_metric.answer: Per-region Z-scores relative to GPR predictions; total outlier count (tOC); extreme negative deviation via deviation rate > 0.2 (for mapping)

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Multiple analyses: (1) Pearson correlations linking tOC to behavior (social problems r=0.31, p=0.001; withdrawal behaviors r=0.28, p=0.001); (2) Ridge regression with nested 5-fold CV (101 repeats) predicting behavior from cerebellar volume deviations, with linear regression within folds adjusting for age and sex (social problems r=0.27, p=0.007; withdrawal r=0.25, p=0.015); (3) Multiple regression assessed clinical covariates' associations with tOC (tumor volume positively associated: r=0.41, p<0.001).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Patients show widespread negative cerebellar deviations; higher tOC and reduced cerebellar volumes associate with greater social problems and withdrawal behaviors.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Over 95% of patients exhibited negative deviations in cerebellar regions, especially anterior lobules (e.g., Left V). tOC correlated with social problems (r=0.31, p=0.001) and withdrawal behaviors (r=0.28, p=0.001). Ridge regression using deviation features predicted social problems (r=0.27, p=0.007) and withdrawal (r=0.25, p=0.015). Tumor volume correlated with tOC (r=0.41, p<0.001). Feature weights were predominantly negative, indicating smaller lobular volumes linked to worse symptoms (e.g., Right X, Right V/IV, Left IX/VIII/X for social problems; Left V, Right IV, Vermis VI/VIII for withdrawal).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: ACAPULCO-based cerebellar parcellation with manual QC; ComBat harmonization (age/gender/TIV covariates); GPR normative percentiles; tOC summarization; ridge regression with nested CV and permutation testing; use of predictive uncertainty from GPR to parameterize centiles.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Normative model included only age and gender; did not account for education or home environment. Behavioral questionnaire (CBCL) focused mainly on social problems and lacked depth for social function. Findings are correlational and do not establish causality.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Healthy control sources and counts: 61 scanned locally in Beijing (of 72 recruited), 69 fcon_1000.projects (doi:10.15387/fcp_indi.corr.ipcas7), 450 CCNP, 269 Children's Hospital Guangzhou (total 849). Ethical and data governance: IRB approvals (KY 2019-124-02; KY 2019124-02); data processed and stored in China; no export of human genetic materials or data.
